title: When Does Wegovy Start Working?
summary: Find out how long Wegovy takes to work, what to expect each month, and which habits support the best weight loss results. - Aug 24, 2026
body_markdown:
If you're a few weeks into treatment and wondering why the scale isn't moving, you're not alone. Most men expect fast results, but weight loss on this type of treatment builds slowly alongside the dose. What's actually happening in the body during those early weeks is worth understanding before you decide it isn't working.


**TLDR:**


- Most men notice appetite changes within 1 to 2 weeks; meaningful weight loss typically builds in months 2 to 3 as the dose increases; clinical trial data shows an average of approximately 14.9% body weight reduction by 68 weeks.1
- Weight loss treatments in this category work by slowing digestion and signalling fullness; results build gradually, not on day one.
- About 44% of participants at higher doses reported nausea in clinical trials2; for most men, side effects ease within days to a few weeks.
- A stalled scale typically points to titration phase timing, no calorie deficit, or underlying conditions like hypothyroidism.
- Pair treatment with adequate daily protein intake and sufficient sleep to support results. Your provider can help set targets based on your body weight and health goals.


## How Wegovy Works in the Body


Weight management treatments like[Wegovy](https://www.phoenix.ca/medications/wegovy) work by mimicking a hormone the body already produces. That hormone plays a role in appetite and digestion, which is why treatments built around it can support weight management as part of a broader plan.


Once in the system, this treatment signals areas of the brain involved in hunger and fullness. It also slows gastric emptying, meaning food stays in the stomach longer than usual. That slower digestion is a big part of why appetite changes build gradually and not all at once.


The body needs time to adjust to the new hormone signal these treatments introduce, and the dose escalation schedule reflects that. Expecting an immediate shift on day one sets you up for disappointment, since appetite and fullness signals typically become more noticeable over the following weeks as your provider adjusts your plan.


## The Wegovy Dose Escalation Schedule


Wegovy follows a gradual titration schedule designed to let your body adjust to each dose before moving higher. The escalation unfolds gradually, with your provider determining when to advance based on how your body responds. Each increase brings a stronger appetite-suppressing effect, which is why weight loss tends to accelerate as you move through the schedule instead of hitting a peak in week one.


Side effects like nausea and bloating are most common in the days after each dose increase, then tend to ease before the next step up. If you experience side effects that feel difficult to manage, your licensed healthcare provider may recommend staying at your current dose longer before advancing. This is a normal part of the process and does not mean treatment is not working. The goal of titration is to reach the highest dose your body tolerates well, since higher maintenance doses are associated with greater average weight loss in clinical data.


## What to Expect in the First Week and First Month


In the first week, the body is adjusting to a new hormone signal, not actively dropping weight. Nausea tends to peak in the 8 to 24 hours after the first dose, then eases. Some men notice a reduced urge to finish meals within the first few days, while energy levels can dip slightly as the body adapts. Appetite suppression at this stage is subtle: a mild reduction in hunger cues, not a dramatic shift. Most men do not lose more than 1 to 3 lbs in the first two weeks, and that is normal and expected at the starting dose.


By the end of the first month, appetite changes tend to become more noticeable as your provider follows the gradual titration schedule. Portion sizes that once felt routine may now feel like too much, and cravings between meals often ease. Some men see modest weight movement in the first four weeks; others see little change until the dose steps up. Neither outcome signals a problem. Meaningful results build across the titration period, not from the first injection.


On the lifestyle side, the first month is a good time to build the habits that support treatment: eating smaller meals, staying hydrated, and building adequate daily protein intake to protect muscle as the scale eventually starts to move. Your provider can help you set a protein target that fits your body weight and health goals. What you do in these early weeks lays the groundwork for stronger results later in the process.

## Month-by-Month Weight Loss Results Timeline


Results vary between individuals, but clinical data gives a reasonable picture of what to expect as you move through the titration schedule. In months one and two, weight loss is typically modest: most men are still on lower doses, appetite changes are just beginning, and the body is adapting to a new hormone signal. The STEP 1 trial suggests average losses of roughly 2 to 3% of body weight by week 4, rising to around 8 to 9% by week 20.1 These are rough benchmarks, not guarantees, since individual results vary. Some see the scale barely move at this stage, which is normal and expected.


Months two through four tend to mark a turning point. As your dose increases, appetite suppression becomes more noticeable, portions naturally shrink, and a consistent calorie deficit becomes easier to maintain. This is when most men start to see steady week-over-week movement on the scale. By months four to six, you've typically reached or are approaching the maintenance dose, and weight loss tends to be at its most consistent:[NEJM clinical trial data](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2032183) shows a mean body weight reduction of ~14.9% at 68 weeks for those who stay on track with both treatment and lifestyle habits.1


Beyond six months, results continue to accumulate with consistent use, though the rate of loss can plateau as your body adapts. If weight stalls at this stage, your licensed healthcare provider can review your dose and habits to determine whether adjustments make sense. The overall pattern across these months reinforces a key point: meaningful results build gradually alongside the titration schedule, not from the first injection.


## Common Side Effects and When They Improve


The most common side effects with weight loss treatments in this category involve digestion: nausea, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, bloating, headache, and fatigue. Nausea is usually the first one people notice. In clinical trials, about[44%](https://www.wegovy.com/obesity/is-wegovy-right-for-me/safety-side-effects.html) of participants at the higher maintenance dose reported nausea.2


These effects tend to peak during the early weeks of treatment and again after each dose increase, as your body adjusts to a new signal. For a closer look, see this[GLP-1 and semaglutide side effects week-by-week guide](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/glp1-semaglutide-side-effects-week-week) . For most men, symptoms ease within days to a few weeks.


A few habits can help:


- Eat smaller meals instead of large ones
- Skip fatty or spicy foods while you adjust
- Stay hydrated throughout the day
- Eat slowly and stop before you feel overly full


If side effects feel severe or do not ease with time, flag it with your provider instead of pushing through alone.


## Serious Side Effects to Know Before Starting


Beyond digestive discomfort, weight loss treatments in this category carry warnings that deserve attention before you start.


Pancreatitis, or inflammation of the pancreas, is one risk to watch for. Severe stomach pain that spreads to your back, along with nausea or vomiting, needs prompt medical evaluation. Gallbladder problems are another concern, since rapid weight changes can increase the chance of gallstones forming. Kidney issues can also develop, often tied to dehydration from ongoing nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea, so staying hydrated matters more than it might seem.


There is also a boxed warning tied to a potential risk of thyroid C-cell tumors, based on animal studies, as noted in the prescribing information. Because of this, these treatments are not appropriate for anyone with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2.


A licensed healthcare provider should review your full medical history before you start treatment and stay involved throughout, so warning signs get caught early.


## Why You May Not Be Losing Weight on Wegovy


Weight not moving usually comes down to a handful of factors. Here is what tends to explain a stall.


- Still in the titration phase (the gradual dose increase period). Weight loss builds as your dose rises, so a slower start at lower doses is normal.
- No calorie deficit. Appetite may be more manageable, but weight loss still depends on eating less than you burn.
- Inconsistent dosing or technique. Missed or skipped doses can blunt results; if unsure how to handle a missed dose, check with your licensed healthcare provider before your next scheduled dose. Doubling up is not recommended, and repeated gaps in dosing can delay progress through titration and push back your results timeline.
- Underlying health conditions. Hypothyroidism and insulin resistance can slow how your body responds.
- Stress and poor sleep. Both raise cortisol and hunger hormones, working against your efforts.
- Individual metabolic differences. Genetics affect how quickly, and how much, any one person responds.


[Weight loss plateaus](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/weight-loss-plateau-men) are a normal part of this process, not a sign that treatment has stopped working. If your weight stalls for several weeks despite sticking to your plan, bring it up with your provider so they can review your dose and habits together.


## How to Maximize Weight Loss Results on Wegovy


Weight loss treatments in this category work best paired with lifestyle habits, not instead of them. Providers prescribe them alongside a reduced calorie diet and regular physical activity, so what you do outside of treatment still shapes results.


A few habits consistently support stronger outcomes:


- Keep a calorie deficit.
- Eat enough protein. Learn[daily protein intake for weight loss](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/how-much-protein-per-day-to-lose-weight-without-losing-muscle) : eating adequate protein daily helps preserve muscle mass as the scale drops. Your provider can recommend a target based on your body weight.
- [Exercise and lifestyle changes for weight loss](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/maximizing-weight-loss-with-glp-1) matter, and strength training combined with cardio supports fat loss and the muscle you want to keep.
- Prioritize quality sleep each night.[Sleep and weight gain in men](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/sleep-weight-gain-men) are closely linked, and poor sleep raises hunger hormones and works against your progress.
- Stay hydrated. Water supports digestion and can ease some nausea.
- Track your progress. Monthly photos and follow-up consults with your provider help spot trends the scale might miss.


These habits work alongside treatment, not in place of it.


## Accessing Weight Loss Treatment Through a Men's Online Health Clinic in Canada


Men's online health clinics connect Canadian men with licensed healthcare providers who can assess eligibility for weight management treatment. The process typically starts with a confidential online health assessment that covers your medical history, current health conditions, and weight management goals. A licensed healthcare provider reviews that information and, if treatment is clinically appropriate, issues a prescription that ships in plain, discreet packaging directly to your door.


This model is available across much of Canada, including Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta, Manitoba, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island. For men in rural areas or those without easy access to a regular care provider, this kind of access can make a meaningful difference in getting a weight management plan started. Once treatment is underway, ongoing support through secure messaging means you can flag side effects, ask questions, or request guidance without scheduling a separate appointment.


## Final Thoughts on Wegovy Results and What Shapes Them


Weight loss on this type of treatment is a gradual process, and individual results vary based on dose, habits, and how your body responds. Side effects tend to ease with time, and plateaus are a normal part of the process. Keeping your provider in the loop means you always have support to adjust your approach when needed.


## FAQ


### How long does it take for this weight loss treatment to work?


Appetite changes typically begin within 1 to 2 weeks, with meaningful weight loss building over months 2 to 3 as your dose increases. Clinical trial data shows average weight loss results continue to improve through the titration period (the gradual dose escalation phase), so the first month rarely reflects your full potential results. Expecting no movement on the scale in week one is completely normal.


### Why am I not losing weight on my weight loss treatment even after several weeks?


Slower results in the early weeks are expected: weight loss builds as your dose rises through titration. A calorie deficit still needs to be present for the treatment to produce results, and factors like poor sleep, high stress, inconsistent dosing, or underlying conditions such as hypothyroidism can all blunt your progress.


### What should you expect in the first week on this weight loss treatment?


Dramatic weight loss is unlikely in the first week; the starting dose is intentionally low as the body adjusts to a new hormone signal. Nausea is the most commonly reported side effect early on and tends to peak in the first few weeks before easing for most men. Eating smaller meals, staying hydrated, and avoiding fatty or spicy foods can help you get through the adjustment period more comfortably.


### Do Wegovy side effects go away over time?


For most men, digestive side effects like nausea, bloating, and fatigue ease within days to a few weeks as your body adjusts. Side effects tend to return briefly after each dose increase, then settle again. If symptoms feel severe or persistent, flag them with your licensed healthcare provider instead of pushing through alone. Adjustments to your plan are possible.


### What are 5 ways to increase weight loss results on this treatment?


Pairing your treatment with consistent lifestyle habits produces stronger results than relying on the prescription alone. The five habits that consistently move the needle are: maintaining a calorie deficit, eating enough protein daily to preserve muscle mass (your provider can set a target based on your body weight), combining strength training with cardio, prioritizing sufficient sleep each night to keep hunger hormones in check, and tracking progress monthly through photos and follow-up check-ins with your licensed healthcare provider.
